daad-doctoral-programmes-germany-2028.about:
DAAD's Research Grants – Doctoral Programmes in Germany fund international graduates to complete a whole PhD at a German university or research institute, either in an individual doctorate with a supervisor or in a structured doctoral programme.

You need an above-average master's (or, exceptionally, bachelor's) degree completed by the start of funding, normally no more than six years old at the deadline, a research proposal and confirmation of supervision from a German professor. If you have already started a doctorate, it should have begun no more than three years before applying, and you must not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months.

The current round (funding starting 2027) is closed. The portal opens again on 1 June 2027 for funding starting in 2028, with country-specific deadlines that usually follow the previous year's pattern (often autumn). The grant pays €1,400 a month, a €460 annual research allowance, insurance, travel and German-language support, with rent and family allowances possible.
highlights: €1,400/month for up to 4 years
Insurance, travel, research and language allowances
Next portal opens 1 June 2027
daad-doctoral-programmes-germany-2028.eligibility: Mainly nationals of developing and emerging countries listed in the DAAD database for this programme (check your country of origin in the database). Above-average master's degree completed by funding start, normally not more than six years old; supervision agreement from a German host; not more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the deadline. Medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine follow separate rules.
how_to_apply: Find a supervisor or structured doctoral programme in Germany and obtain written confirmation
Check your country's deadline in the DAAD scholarship database from June 2027
Register in the DAAD portal and generate the recommendation form for a professor
Upload CV, motivation letter, research proposal, supervision letter, degrees and transcripts
Submit before 24:00 CET on your deadline
daad-doctoral-programmes-germany-2028.costs: €1,400 per month, €460 per year research allowance, health/accident/liability insurance contributions, travel allowance on request, language course costs, plus possible monthly rent subsidy and family allowance.

daad-epos-2027.about:
EPOS (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses) is a DAAD scholarship scheme funded by the German development ministry (BMZ). It pays for professionals from developing and emerging countries to complete selected English- (and some German-) taught master's courses in Germany, such as International Health (Charité Berlin, Heidelberg), Global Health (Bonn), Urban Management (TU Berlin), Hydro Science (TU Dresden), Renewable Energy (Oldenburg, Flensburg), Agricultural Economics (Hohenheim) and Environmental Governance (Freiburg).

It targets people already working in their field: you need a four-year bachelor's in the upper third of your class, at least two years of relevant work experience, and a degree normally no more than six years old. You apply directly to up to three courses, which select candidates and propose them to DAAD.

Graduates receive €992 a month (doctoral candidates in some courses €1,400), insurance and a travel allowance, with possible rent and family subsidies. Each course sets its own deadline, listed in DAAD's EPOS deadline list; many 2027/28 deadlines closed in autumn 2026, so check each course and plan for the 2028/29 round.
highlights: €992/month plus insurance and travel for master's students
About 25 development-focused courses across Germany
Requires 2+ years of professional experience
daad-epos-2027.eligibility: Residents of countries on DAAD's EPOS country list (based on the OECD DAC list of developing countries; Georgia is a DAC country, high-income Qatar is not), so check the list before applying. Bachelor's degree (normally four years) in the upper third, at least two years of relevant work experience after it, degree normally not older than six years, not more than 15 months in Germany at the deadline, and English/German proof (IELTS or TOEFL, institutional TOEFL not accepted).
how_to_apply: Check the EPOS country list and the 2027/28 course list and deadline list on the DAAD website
Pick up to three courses and rank them in the DAAD form
Send the checklist, EPOS form, Europass CV, one motivation letter, employer recommendation, employment certificates, language proof and degrees directly to the course(s)
If the course selects you, DAAD asks you to upload documents to its portal
daad-epos-2027.costs: €992 per month for master's students (€1,400 for doctoral candidates), health/accident/liability insurance contributions, travel allowance, and in some cases rent subsidy and family allowance. EPOS scholars are exempt from tuition fees in courses that charge them (e.g. Freiburg).

vliruos-icp-connect-2027.about:
VLIR-UOS, the development-cooperation arm of the Flemish universities, funds full scholarships for selected International Courses Programmes (ICP) taught in English in Belgium. For 2027–2028 the funded master's programmes include Aquaculture (IMAQUA, Ghent), Food Technology (KU Leuven & Ghent), Marine and Lacustrine Science (VUB, Ghent, Antwerp), Transportation Sciences – Road Safety (Hasselt), Nutrition and Food Systems (Ghent), Sustainable Land Management (Ghent & VUB), Tropical Biodiversity and Ecosystems (VUB, TROPIMUNDO), and one-year advanced master's programmes at the University of Antwerp in Development Evaluation, Globalisation and Development, and Governance and Development.

The scheme prefers candidates working in (or aiming for) higher education, government or civil society who will act as agents of change at home; women are encouraged to apply. Initial-master candidates must be 35 or younger on 1 January 2027 (advanced master's: 45 or younger).

You apply to the programme and tick the scholarship request in the same application. Deadlines differ: 30 November 2026 for TROPIMUNDO, 1 February 2027 for several programmes and 28 February 2027 for others. Results come by mid-May; there are no partial scholarships.
highlights: Full package: tuition, travel, insurance, board and lodging
Around 10 English-taught programmes at Flemish universities
Most deadlines between 30 Nov 2026 and 28 Feb 2027
vliruos-icp-connect-2027.eligibility: Nationals and residents of one of 25 countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Morocco, Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, Philippines and Vietnam. Age 35 or under (initial master) or 45 or under (advanced master) on 1 January 2027. One ICP application per year; no previous Belgian government scholarship or enrolment in Belgian higher education. Not open to Georgian or Qatari citizens.
how_to_apply: Check the eligible country list and the 2027–2028 programme list on vliruos.be
Open the programme page and note its own deadline
Apply to the programme through the university and request the VLIR-UOS scholarship in the same application
Apply to only one ICP programme
Join the online info session on 26 November 2026 if useful
vliruos-icp-connect-2027.costs: Covers tuition, international travel, insurance and living expenses (board and lodging) for the full 12, 24 or 36 months. No partial scholarships.

kas-international-scholarship-2027.about:
The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, a German political foundation, supports about 300 international scholars from more than 50 countries. Its international talent programme funds four-semester master's degrees and full doctorates at German universities, alongside seminars on politics, society and leadership.

It looks for academic excellence plus social or volunteer engagement (ideally in your home country), commitment to democracy and human rights, and interest in political questions. German at B2 level is expected by the start of studies, even for English-taught programmes. There is no age limit; medicine and three-semester master's programmes are not funded.

Applicants already living in Germany apply via the KAS Campus portal by 15 July each year (12:00 CET). Selected KAS offices abroad also recruit; check the website for the current list.
highlights: Up to €992/month (master's) or €1,400/month (PhD)
Seminars and a network of ~300 international scholars
Annual deadline 15 July
kas-international-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Mainly non-EU international students. Master's applicants must plan a four-semester master's at a German university; doctoral applicants must be fully admitted to a German doctorate. German at B2 by the start of studies. Strong academic record, civic engagement and commitment to democratic values. Not for medicine, state-exam dentistry or postdocs.
how_to_apply: Read the KAS guidelines and FAQ
Secure (or apply for) admission to a German master's or doctoral programme
Register on the KAS Campus portal (campus.kas.de)
Upload CV, motivation letter, transcripts, references and proof of engagement
Submit by 15 July, 12:00 CET (or via a participating KAS office abroad)
kas-international-scholarship-2027.costs: Up to €992 per month (master's) or €1,400 per month (doctorate); optional health insurance subsidy (up to €120/month), family and child allowances, research travel grants, and in exceptional cases up to €750 per semester toward tuition. Semester fees are not covered.

slovak-national-scholarship-programme-20.about:
The National Scholarship Programme of the Slovak Republic (NSP), administered by SAIA for the Slovak Ministry of Education, funds mobility stays in Slovakia for international university students, PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists. Master's and PhD students typically come for one or two semesters of study or research while remaining enrolled at their home university.

You need an invitation or acceptance letter from a Slovak university or research institution, a study or research plan and a recommendation from your supervisor. The scholarship is a monthly payment intended to cover living costs (accommodation and meals); travel is usually not included.

The programme runs two calls a year. The call for the summer semester of 2026/27 closes on 31 October 2026, and the earlier call closed on 30 April 2026, so the next round for the 2027/28 academic year is expected to close on 30 April 2027.
highlights: Monthly living stipend for a semester or two in Slovakia
For master's students, PhD students and researchers
Two calls a year (30 April / 31 October)
slovak-national-scholarship-programme-20.eligibility: International university students (in at least their 3rd year, including master's), PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists from abroad, with an acceptance or invitation letter from a Slovak host institution. Open to most nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar; see the programme's terms and conditions for country-specific rules.
how_to_apply: Find a Slovak university or research institute and obtain an acceptance/invitation letter
Prepare a study or research plan, CV, recommendation and transcripts
Submit the online application on scholarships.sk before the deadline
Wait for the selection committee's decision (published list of scholarship holders)
slovak-national-scholarship-programme-20.costs: Monthly scholarship to cover living costs in Slovakia (amounts by category in the programme's terms and conditions). Travel costs are generally not covered. No tuition is charged for the exchange stay.

isdb-scholarships-2027-2028.about:
The Islamic Development Bank runs several scholarship programmes for its 57 member countries and Muslim communities elsewhere. Two are graduate-level. The M.Sc. Scholarship Program for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries funds master's study in science, engineering, technology, medicine, Islamic finance, project and procurement management, entrepreneurship, supply chain and public policy for citizens of 20 LDMCs, at universities in IsDB member countries ranked in the THE top 1,000. The Merit Scholarship Program for High Technology (MSP) funds three-year PhDs and 6–12 month postdoctoral research for scholars attached to universities or research centres in member countries.

Both programmes pay tuition directly to the university, a monthly stipend matched to local living costs, medical costs, a thesis allowance, return airfare and an installation allowance. MSP applicants are nominated at the institutional level and must return to their institution afterwards.

The 2027–2028 booklets are already published, and applications are submitted online through the IsDB scholarship portal during the application period. Apply to only one programme per cycle.
highlights: Tuition, monthly stipend, medical, thesis allowance and flights
Master's for 20 least developed member countries; PhD for all member countries
2027–2028 booklets published; apply via the IsDB portal
isdb-scholarships-2027-2028.eligibility: M.Sc.: citizens of 20 IsDB Least Developed Member Countries (Afghanistan, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Comoros, Djibouti, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Maldives, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Palestine, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Togo, Uganda, Yemen), aged 30 or under, with a science/technology bachelor's, above-average grades and relevant work experience. MSP (PhD/postdoc): scholars from any IsDB member country who work at an educational, scientific or research institution at home, in priority high-tech fields. Qatar is an IsDB member; Georgia is not.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027–2028 booklet for your programme from isdb.org
Secure admission at an eligible university (THE/QS top 1,000 in an IsDB member country, or a partner university)
Register on the IsDB scholarship portal and complete the online application
Upload documents and submit before the cycle's deadline; some applicants are interviewed
isdb-scholarships-2027-2028.costs: Covers tuition (paid to the university), monthly stipend set by country cost of living, medical treatment/insurance, thesis or research-paper allowance, conference allowance for PhD scholars, return air ticket and installation allowance. Visa costs and family expenses are not covered.

rhodes-scholarship-2028.about:
The Rhodes Scholarship, founded in 1902, brings exceptional young people from around the world to the University of Oxford for postgraduate study. Scholars can take most full-time master's and doctoral courses in almost any field, and join a residential community at Rhodes House focused on leadership and service.

Selection is by constituency: many countries and regions have their own Rhodes Scholarships, and applicants from countries without one can apply for the Global Rhodes Scholarships. Candidates are judged on academic excellence, character, leadership and commitment to others, with interviews for finalists.

The award covers Oxford fees, an annual stipend (£20,400 in 2025-26), the application fee, visa and health surcharge, two economy flights and a settling-in allowance; a DPhil can be funded for up to three years. Applications for 2027 entry are closed; they reopen in 2027 for 2028 entry.
highlights: Oxford fees + £20,400/year stipend + flights and visa costs
Most Oxford master's and DPhil courses
Applications reopen in 2027 for 2028 entry
rhodes-scholarship-2028.eligibility: Depends on constituency: each country or region (and the Global Rhodes Scholarship for countries without their own) sets citizenship/residency, age and degree requirements. Check 'Check your eligibility' on the Rhodes House website when applications reopen. Both Georgian and Qatari citizens can check eligibility under their regional or the Global constituency.
how_to_apply: Sign up to the Rhodes House mailing list for the 2027 opening
Check which constituency you belong to and its eligibility rules
Prepare a personal statement, academic statement, CV, transcripts and references
Apply online by your constituency's deadline (typically July–October 2027)
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; scholars then apply to their Oxford course
rhodes-scholarship-2028.costs: Covers Oxford course fees, an annual stipend of £20,400 (£1,700/month, 2025-26 rate), the Oxford application fee, student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, two economy flights and a settling-in allowance.

tropimundo-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
TROPIMUNDO (Mundus Tropicalis) is a two-year master's in tropical biodiversity and ecosystems. Semester 1 is in Brussels (ULB and VUB), semester 2 is field experience in a tropical region (partners in Kenya, Senegal, Benin, Cameroon, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, the Philippines, French Guiana, New Caledonia and more), semester 3 is a specialisation at Sorbonne/MNHN in Paris or the University of Florence, and semester 4 is the thesis.

It suits biology, natural science and environmental science graduates (about 180 ECTS) with good English, plus French or Spanish as a bonus.

The first call, for scholarship seekers, closes on 30 November 2026. Students from VLIR-UOS countries can receive a full VLIR-UOS scholarship; Erasmus Mundus scholarships for all nationalities depend on European Commission approval. Self-funded applicants can apply from February to 30 April 2027 (tuition €9,000 a year for non-associated third-country students, €4,500 for EU and associated countries).
highlights: Field semester in tropical Africa, Asia or South America
VLIR-UOS full scholarships; Erasmus Mundus scholarships pending EC approval
Scholarship deadline 30 November 2026
tropimundo-erasmus-mundus-2027.eligibility: Bachelor of Science (about 180 ECTS) in biology, natural sciences, environmental sciences or equivalent; English proficiency (French and/or Spanish useful). VLIR-UOS scholarships only for nationals/residents of the 25 VLIR-UOS countries; Erasmus Mundus scholarships (if funded) open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Register on the TROPIMUNDO application form
Upload diploma, transcripts, language proof, CV and motivation letter
Indicate that you are a scholarship seeker (VLIR-UOS and/or Erasmus Mundus)
Submit by 30 November 2026
tropimundo-erasmus-mundus-2027.costs: Tuition: €9,000 per year (non-associated third countries) or €4,500 per year (EU and Erasmus+ associated countries). VLIR-UOS scholarships cover tuition, travel, insurance and living costs; Erasmus Mundus scholarships (if funded) follow the EU standard of €1,400 per month plus participation costs.

z-fellows.about:
Z Fellows is a short, intense programme for early-stage technical builders. Each cohort spends one week, mostly online, meeting founders of very large technology companies, getting feedback on what they are building and joining a network that stays with them for the life of their company. The last day is held in person in San Francisco or New York.

There is no age limit and no need to have a registered company or to quit school or a job: past fellows include high-school students, undergraduates, dropouts, recent graduates and people in full-time work. You can apply alone or with co-founders (one application per team).

The programme is free. Fellows may also accept a $10,000 investment on a $1B valuation cap, which converts into stock at the next priced round, so it costs almost nothing in equity. It is one of the lightest-touch ways for a young builder to get access to top Silicon Valley founders.
highlights: Free one-week programme, mostly virtual, final day in San Francisco or New York
Optional $10,000 investment at a $1B valuation cap
No age limit; high-school and university students welcome
z-fellows.eligibility: Open worldwide to technical builders of any age, including high-school and university students and dropouts. You do not need a company yet. Teams submit one application. Programme language is English.
how_to_apply: Go to zfellows.com and click 'Apply Now'
Describe what you are building and your technical background; list co-founders in the same form
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; shortlisted applicants are interviewed
Rejected applicants may reapply later
z-fellows.costs: Free to take part. Optional $10,000 investment (converts at a $1B cap). Travel to the in-person final day may be at your own cost; check with the organisers.

emergent-ventures.about:
Emergent Ventures (EV) is a fellowship and grant programme at the Mercatus Center at George Mason University, led by economist Tyler Cowen. It backs individuals with 'zero to one' ideas that could improve society: a startup, a research project, a piece of writing, a non-profit, or simply time and travel to develop a talent. Many winners are teenagers and university students.

Besides the general programme, EV has dedicated tranches for Africa and the Caribbean, India, Ukraine, UK dynamism, archaeology, US science policy and travel for career development. Grants are decided quickly with very little bureaucracy, and recipients join a strong global network of past winners.

The application is a short online form. Applications written with AI are rejected (AI may only be used for proofreading), so write it yourself and be specific about what you will do with the money.
highlights: Open worldwide from age 13
Any field: startups, research, writing, non-profits, talent development
Special tranches for Africa, India, Ukraine and others
emergent-ventures.eligibility: Anyone aged 13 or older, from any country. One application per person and project. Applications must be written by the applicant; AI-written applications are rejected.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page at mercatus.org/emergent-ventures
Open the application form (mercatus.tfaforms.net/5099527)
Explain your project, what you will use the grant for and why it matters
Submit once; the team cannot give feedback or status updates
emergent-ventures.costs: Free to apply. Grant size depends on the project and is not published.

1517-medici-project.about:
The Medici Project is the grant arm of the 1517 Fund, a venture firm that backs dropouts, students and deep-tech scientists. It gives a minimum $1,000 stipend, with no equity or IP taken, to young people building something in any field: science, technology, maths or the arts. It is not a prize for past work but a bet on what you will do next, and the project must not be for school grades or admissions.

Applying is informal: you send a five-minute video about who you are, why the project matters to you and how the money would help. Grants are paid quickly. Recipients often stay in touch with the 1517 community, which also invests in startups founded by young people.

Note: because of international regulations, grants are restricted to teams in North America; others may write in, but support may be limited.
highlights: At least $1,000, no strings and no equity taken
Any field, including science and the arts
Simple video application, answer within about two weeks
1517-medici-project.eligibility: High-school students, university students and dropouts. Grants are limited to teams based in North America; applicants elsewhere can contact the team but direct funding may not be possible.
how_to_apply: Record a five-minute Loom video: who you are, your project, how the grant would help
Email it to a 1517 team member (firstname@1517fund.com) or use the 'Get in Touch' form on 1517fund.com
Wait for a reply (about two weeks for in-thesis submissions)
1517-medici-project.costs: Free to apply. Grant of at least $1,000, paid directly.

antler-residency.about:
Antler runs founder residencies in cities across Asia-Pacific (Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Bangalore, Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur, Ho Chi Minh City, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane), the Americas (San Francisco, New York, Austin, Toronto, São Paulo), Europe (London, Amsterdam/Berlin, Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo, Helsinki), the Middle East (Dubai, Riyadh) and Africa (Lagos, Nairobi). Founders join a cohort, test ideas, meet potential co-founders and pitch Antler's investment committee for pre-seed capital.

Upcoming cohort start dates published on Antler's site: Tokyo 2 November 2026; Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne 8 February 2027; Lagos and Seoul 15 March 2027; Nairobi 22 March 2027. Toronto, San Francisco, Austin, New York and the Nordic cities take founders on a rolling basis. These are start dates, not deadlines, so apply early.

It suits recent graduates and young professionals who want to start a company but do not yet have a co-founder. Investment terms vary by location and are explained during the process.
highlights: Programmes in 25+ cities on five continents
Apply solo or as a team, even at idea stage
Pre-seed investment for teams that pass investment committee
antler-residency.eligibility: Aspiring founders (usually 18+ with work or technical experience); you can apply as an individual without a co-founder or idea. Each location sets its own requirements (right to work, residence). Language: English.
how_to_apply: Go to antler.co/apply
Fill in your details and choose your stage (Idea to Pre-Seed), region and city
Check cohort start dates on antler.co/cohort-start-dates
If shortlisted, complete interviews with the local team
antler-residency.costs: No fee to join. Antler invests in companies in exchange for equity; terms differ by city. Living costs during the residency are usually your own.

techstars-anywhere-2027.about:
Techstars is one of the world's best-known accelerator networks. Techstars Anywhere is its remote-first programme: founders keep working from home, take part online in mentorship, workshops and investor preparation, and travel to three in-person offsites in startup hubs. The programme starts on 8 March 2027 and ends with Demo Day on 3 June 2027.

The 2027 cohort looks for domain experts building valuable technology across industries, with a particular emphasis on robotics, energy, applied and physical AI and materials science. It is designed for companies working in North American time zones, but there is no relocation requirement.

Selected companies receive Techstars investment (terms are given on the application portal), lifetime access to the Techstars network of mentors, alumni and investors, and perks worth large sums in software credits. It suits student or graduate founders who already have a product or prototype.
highlights: Remote-first, no relocation, three in-person offsites
Focus on robotics, energy, applied AI and materials
Demo Day 3 June 2027 in front of investors
techstars-anywhere-2027.eligibility: Startup founders with a product or strong technical prototype, any nationality; the programme runs on North American time zones. Apply as a company team.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page at techstars.com/accelerators/anywhere
Create an account at apply.techstars.com and choose Techstars Anywhere
Submit the application (team, product, traction, video) by 18 November 2026
Shortlisted teams interview with the managing director
techstars-anywhere-2027.costs: No fee. Techstars invests in each company in exchange for equity (see the application portal for current terms). Offsite travel may be at the company's expense.

hello-tomorrow-global-challenge-2027.about:
The Hello Tomorrow Global Challenge, now in its 12th edition, selects the most promising science-based startups in the world. There are twelve industry tracks (computing and cybersecurity, aerospace, mobility, climate tech, digital health and medtech, energy, agri-food, industrial AI and robotics, industrial biotech, new materials and green chemistry, medical biotech and pharma, semiconductors) plus a cross-cutting 'Spinout Breakthroughs' track for university spin-outs.

Timeline: applications 23 September to 30 November 2026; 'Deep Tech Pioneers' selected in February 2027; finalists announced in April 2027; Investor Day with 350+ investors on 1 June 2027 and the Summit and Challenge Finals on 2–3 June 2027 in Amsterdam. Selected Pioneers get exposure to investors, corporates and media; the top prize is a €200,000 equity investment from DeepBright Ventures, and there is a dedicated prize for idea and pre-seed teams.

Ideal for student and PhD researchers turning lab work into a company.
highlights: €200,000 equity prize plus an early-stage prize
13 tracks covering all major deep-tech fields
Finals in Amsterdam before 350+ investors
hello-tomorrow-global-challenge-2027.eligibility: Startups from early development up to Series B built on a new technology, scientific discovery or complex engineering; at least two team members; not a subsidiary of an existing company. Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Read the rules at hello-tomorrow.org/global-challenge
Choose the track that fits your technology
Submit the online application by 30 November 2026
Optional: join the 'Ask Me Anything' info sessions
Pioneers are announced in February 2027, finalists in April 2027
hello-tomorrow-global-challenge-2027.costs: Free to apply. Finalists' attendance at the Summit is supported by the organisers; check the rules for travel coverage.

microsoft-for-startups.about:
Microsoft for Startups (formerly the Founders Hub) is a self-serve programme that helps early-stage companies build on Microsoft's cloud. Members can receive up to $150,000 in credits for eligible Azure services, access to leading AI models and tools, technical documentation and guidance, and free access to selected software and platforms. Credits can be used from early development all the way to production workloads.

There is no cohort and no deadline: you sign up online, describe your startup and unlock benefits in stages as your company grows. It is particularly useful for student founders building AI or software products who need cloud computing without paying for it.

Credit levels and requirements change from time to time, so check the current terms on the official page when you register.
highlights: Up to $150,000 in Azure credits
Access to AI models, developer tools and technical guidance
Free, online and open year-round
microsoft-for-startups.eligibility: Early-stage startups and founders worldwide; requirements for each credit tier are shown during sign-up (a Microsoft account and a description of your product are needed). Must be 18+ to accept the terms.
how_to_apply: Go to microsoft.com/startups and click 'Get started now'
Sign in with a Microsoft account and describe your startup
Accept the terms and activate your first tier of benefits
Unlock larger credit tiers as your startup progresses

anzisha-prize-2027.about:
The Anzisha Prize, run by the African Leadership Academy in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, backs young African changemakers with funding, coaching and a platform. Since its launch it has supported 300+ fellows from more than 35 African countries and distributed over $2 million.

The 2027 intake is a multi-year fellowship designed to strengthen fellows' ventures, accelerate growth and create jobs. It is not for ideas: you must already have started your business, social project or invention and be able to show real activity such as customers, sales or beneficiaries. The business does not need to be registered and can be in any sector.

Application is free. It is one of the very few serious entrepreneurship awards designed specifically for teenagers.
highlights: For founders aged 15–22 only
Multi-year fellowship with funding and coaching
Free application; any sector, including social ventures
anzisha-prize-2027.eligibility: Citizens of an African country (valid ID or passport), aged 15–22, who are founding members of a business operating in Africa and serving African customers or beneficiaries, with real activity (not just an idea).
how_to_apply: Read the application guide on anzisha.org/apply
Prepare evidence of your venture's activity (customers, sales, beneficiaries)
Submit the free online application by 10 November 2026
Shortlisted applicants go through interviews and due diligence
anzisha-prize-2027.costs: Free to apply. Fellowship support (funding, coaching, events) is provided by the programme.

start-up-chile-big-13.about:
Start-Up Chile, run by Chile's economic development agency CORFO, is one of the world's best-known public accelerators. It gives equity-free funding: founders keep 100% of their company. Programmes: Build, a 4-month pre-acceleration for teams going from a validated idea to an MVP, with 15 million Chilean pesos; Ignite, a 4-month acceleration for startups with a working product and early validation that are under three years old, with 30 million pesos (plus a possible 20 million extension); and Growth for more mature companies. Industry and nationality do not matter, and teams led by women can receive up to 90% financing through the Female Founder Factor.

The BIG 13 generation call opens on 3 November 2026 at 13:00 Chile time. Selected startups usually base themselves in Chile during the programme and join a large international founder community in Santiago.

For students and young founders worldwide it is a rare chance to receive non-dilutive government funding and a Latin American launchpad.
highlights: Equity-free funding: 15M CLP (Build) or 30M CLP (Ignite)
Open to founders of any nationality and industry
Female Founder Factor: up to 90% financing for women-led teams
start-up-chile-big-13.eligibility: Founders from any country. Build: validated idea to early prototype. Ignite: functional product with early validation, company under 3 years old. Check the legal bases for the BIG 13 call for residency and co-financing rules.
how_to_apply: Read the Build, Ignite and Growth pages on startupchile.org
Wait for the BIG 13 call to open on 3 November 2026
Download the legal bases (bases legales) for your programme
Submit the online application with your team, product and pitch
Selected teams relocate to Chile for the programme
start-up-chile-big-13.costs: No fee and no equity. Funding: 15M CLP (Build), 30M CLP (Ignite). Programmes usually require partial co-financing and living in Chile during the programme; see the legal bases.

earth-prize-2027.about:
The Earth Prize, run by The Earth Foundation in Geneva, asks school students to design a solution to an environmental problem (waste, pollution, climate, biodiversity and more) at local, national or global scale. Since 2022 almost 21,000 students from 169 countries and territories have taken part.

2027 timeline: registration closes 10 January 2027; submissions close 31 January 2027; scholar selection in February and announcement on 3 March; a mentored scholar phase in March; regional winner phase in April; regional winners announced 9 May; public voting 10–23 May; awards ceremony 28 May 2027. Seven regional winners (Southeast Asia and Oceania, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, North America, Central and South America) each receive $10,000 to implement their idea, and mentors are also recognised.

Teams receive learning content and mentoring throughout. It is an excellent first 'startup-style' project for high-school students and looks strong on university applications.
highlights: $10,000 for each of seven regional winners
Free, online and open in 169+ countries
Mentoring and learning content for every team
earth-prize-2027.eligibility: Students aged 13–19 enrolled in a secondary school anywhere in the world, usually in teams supported by a teacher mentor. Submissions in English.
how_to_apply: Register your team at theearthprize.org/2027 before 10 January 2027
Find a teacher or adult mentor and choose an environmental problem
Develop your solution using the learning content
Submit your project by 31 January 2027
earth-prize-2027.costs: Free to enter. Prizes: $10,000 per regional winner; $500 for Mentors of the Month.

falling-walls-lab-2027.about:
Falling Walls Lab is part of the Falling Walls Science Summit in Berlin, held around the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall each November. Universities, embassies and research organisations host local Labs around the world. At each one, students and early-career professionals from all disciplines pitch 'which wall' their idea, research project or business could break, in exactly three minutes, to a jury of experts.

Winners of each local Lab (about 100 in total) advance to the Global Finale in Berlin, where they pitch again, meet scientists, investors and leaders, and attend the Falling Walls Science Summit. Many participants are master's or PhD students, but bachelor's students and young entrepreneurs also compete.

Applications for the 2027 season open on 1 February 2027. Each local Lab publishes its own date and deadline on the Falling Walls site, so look for one in your country or region.
highlights: Pitch any idea in three minutes, any discipline
~100 winners go to the Global Finale in Berlin
Network with scientists, investors and leaders at the Science Summit
falling-walls-lab-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's, master's and PhD students and early-career professionals; exact age and degree rules are in the applicant criteria on falling-walls.com. Pitches in English.
how_to_apply: From 1 February 2027, find a local Lab near you on falling-walls.com/lab
Apply online with a short description of your idea before that Lab's deadline
If selected, pitch for three minutes at the local Lab
Local winners are invited to the Global Finale in Berlin in November
falling-walls-lab-2027.costs: Free to apply. Check the applicant FAQ for travel support for Berlin finalists.

founder-institute-online-2027.about:
The Founder Institute (FI), founded in Silicon Valley, helps first-time founders go from idea to traction and first funding through a structured series of business-building sprints, weekly sessions with experienced founders and mentors, and peer accountability. You do not need a co-founder or to quit your job; many participants build part-time.

The fully virtual spring 2027 cohort runs from 17 March to 3 June 2027. FI also runs local chapters in dozens of countries (for example Abuja, Armenia, Bulgaria, Hungary, Croatia, Georgia, Czechia, Chile, Brazil and Australia), so you can choose a nearby city instead.

Graduates join FI's 'Equity Collective', in which founders, mentors and FI share in each other's success, and gain access to FI's investor network and alumni benefits. It suits university students and young professionals with an idea who want structure; it is paid, so compare it with free options first.
highlights: Fully online cohort, 17 Mar – 3 Jun 2027
Structured idea-to-funding methodology with mentors
Chapters in 100+ cities if you prefer local
founder-institute-online-2027.eligibility: Aspiring founders worldwide, usually 18+; idea stage is fine and you can keep your job or studies. Applicants take an entrepreneur aptitude assessment. Programme language for the online cohort: English.
how_to_apply: Go to fi.co/join and choose the 'Fully Virtual' cohort or a local chapter
Complete the application and the entrepreneur DNA assessment
Apply by 8 December 2026 for the early entrance fee
If accepted, pay the entrance fee and sign the programme agreement
founder-institute-online-2027.costs: Entrance fee $1,099 (early, until 8 Dec 2026) or $1,599. Graduates contribute equity to the shared Equity Collective; see FI's programme agreements.

st-gallen-symposium-global-ideas-competi.about:
The St. Gallen Symposium is one of the world's leading intergenerational forums, where senior leaders from business, politics and civil society debate with young 'Leaders of Tomorrow'. The 56th Symposium, on the theme 'Conditional Partnerships', takes place on 28–29 April 2027 at the University of St. Gallen.

The Global Ideas Competition is the main way in for students. The 2027 question is 'What could we solve, if we could agree?': identify a solvable problem that persists because parties cannot agree and propose a novel arrangement that would make solving it more effective. You submit a Solution Brief of up to 1,000 words (judged anonymously) and, if shortlisted, a video explainer of up to three minutes.

Three winners share CHF 20,000, and the top 100 entries become Leaders of Tomorrow with travel, accommodation in student flats and meals covered for the Symposium. Results are announced by mid-March 2027.
highlights: CHF 20,000 prize fund for three winners
Top 100 get an expenses-paid trip to the Symposium
Debate with CEOs, ministers and thought leaders
st-gallen-symposium-global-ideas-competi.eligibility: Enrolled in a master's-level or higher programme at a research university (one that offers a PhD) on 1 February 2027, born in 1997 or later, any field, any nationality. Individual entries only; bachelor's students generally ineligible. English. Any AI use must be declared.
how_to_apply: Read the rules on symposium.org/global-ideas-competition
Write a Solution Brief (max 1,000 words, four sections) answering the 2027 question
Submit online by 1 February 2027 (23:59 UTC-12)
If shortlisted, submit a video explainer of up to three minutes
Results by mid-March 2027; arrange your Swiss visa if invited
st-gallen-symposium-global-ideas-competi.costs: Free to enter. Travel, accommodation and meals covered for the top 100; visa fees and pocket money (about CHF 100–200) at your own cost.

hpair-harvard-conference-2027.about:
The Harvard College Project for Asian and International Relations (HPAIR), founded in 1991, has held 49 conferences in 34 countries and welcomed over 40,000 delegates. Past speakers include heads of state and government, the WHO Director-General and leading CEOs.

The 2027 Harvard Conference runs from 5 to 7 February 2027 on Harvard's campus. Delegates attend keynotes and panels on business, technology, policy, health and culture across Asia and the world, take part in 'impact challenges' solving real problems in small teams with mentors, and join networking events and an international talent night.

The application has two stages: an online form with a CV and short answers, then a video or Zoom interview. Early-bird applicants get a discounted ticket, earlier decisions (useful for US visas) and can apply for merit-based scholarships that cover part or all of travel and lodging.
highlights: Held on Harvard's campus, 5–7 Feb 2027
Speakers include world leaders and CEOs
Scholarships for early-bird applicants, including internationals
hpair-harvard-conference-2027.eligibility: Primarily university students (undergraduate and graduate) from any country; check the FAQ for age requirements. You will need a US visa or ESTA. English.
how_to_apply: Apply at apply.hpair.org (or the link on hpair.org): CV plus short-answer questions
Apply in the early-bird round for the discount and scholarship eligibility
Complete the video or Zoom interview if invited
Register and pay the conference fee; arrange your US visa early
hpair-harvard-conference-2027.costs: Conference fee (discounted for early-bird) covers programming, lunches and the opening dinner. Travel and lodging are the delegate's own cost unless a scholarship is awarded.

one-young-world-summit-tokyo-2027.about:
One Young World gathers about 2,000 young leaders from more than 190 countries each year, with counsellors such as former heads of state, Nobel laureates and business leaders. Delegates attend plenary sessions on climate, health, peace, education and business, give speeches from the main stage if selected as delegate speakers, and join an ambassador community that runs projects worldwide.

The 2026 Summit takes place in Cape Town in November 2026. The 2027 Summit will be held at the Tokyo International Forum, reportedly from 28 September to 1 October 2027. Delegates are usually sent by employers, universities or NGOs that pay the delegate fee, but many fully funded scholarships are offered by One Young World and partner companies. These open several months before the Summit.

Sign up on oneyoungworld.com to be told when 2027 delegate and scholarship applications open.
highlights: ~2,000 delegates from 190+ countries
Fully funded scholarships available each year
First summit in Asia since 2015, at the Tokyo International Forum
one-young-world-summit-tokyo-2027.eligibility: Young leaders aged 18–35 of any nationality who are making an impact in their field. Scholarship criteria vary (some target specific countries, sectors or companies). English.
how_to_apply: Watch oneyoungworld.com/apply for the 2027 delegate and scholarship calls
Ask your university, employer or NGO whether it sponsors delegates
Prepare a CV and short statement about your impact
Apply for a scholarship or as a self-funded/sponsored delegate
one-young-world-summit-tokyo-2027.costs: Delegate packages are paid (usually by a sponsoring organisation); scholarships can cover the fee, travel and accommodation.

ecosoc-youth-forum-2027.about:
The ECOSOC Youth Forum is the UN's flagship annual meeting of young people. It gives youth a platform to talk directly with Member States and other actors, voice their views and concerns and shape the agenda ahead of the High-Level Political Forum on the Sustainable Development Goals. Sessions include plenaries with ministers, regional breakouts and thematic discussions on the SDGs under review that year.

The 2027 Forum takes place at UN Headquarters in New York from 13 to 15 April 2027. Young people take part in three main ways: as members of their country's official youth delegation or as UN Youth Delegates; as representatives of youth organisations and NGOs that hold ECOSOC consultative status or are part of the Major Group for Children and Youth; and online, since sessions are usually webcast and open to virtual participation.

For a student this is the most direct way to see UN policy-making on youth issues up close. Contact your national youth council or the ministry responsible for youth early, as delegations are formed months in advance.
highlights: At UN Headquarters, New York, 13–15 April 2027
Direct dialogue with ministers and UN leaders
Join via a national delegation, an accredited NGO or online
ecosoc-youth-forum-2027.eligibility: Young people (usually 18–29) from any UN Member State, nominated through national youth delegations, accredited youth organisations or the Major Group for Children and Youth. Virtual participation is generally open to all. You need your own US visa for in-person attendance.
how_to_apply: Check the ECOSOC events page for the 2027 concept note and registration
Ask your national youth council or youth ministry about the official delegation
Or join through an NGO with ECOSOC consultative status / the UN Major Group for Children and Youth
Register via the UN's official registration (Indico) once it opens; apply for a US visa early
ecosoc-youth-forum-2027.costs: No participation fee. Travel and accommodation are usually covered by your government, organisation or yourself; there is no general travel grant.

european-youth-event-2027.about:
The European Youth Event (EYE) takes place every two years at the European Parliament in Strasbourg. It brings together thousands of young people from across the EU and beyond to discuss Europe's present and future with MEPs, experts and activists through debates, workshops, hackathons, performances and creative sessions. Ideas collected at EYE are compiled into a report presented to MEPs.

EYE2027 will take place on 18–19 June 2027. The European Parliament has opened a call for active, engaged groups of young people (school classes, youth organisations, informal groups) to apply for a financial contribution toward travel and accommodation; the deadline is 13 November 2026. Groups that are not funded, and individuals, can usually register later when registration opens.

Groups from outside the EU have taken part in past editions; check the call's rules for which countries are eligible for the financial contribution.
highlights: Debate directly with Members of the European Parliament
Financial contribution available for selected youth groups
Thousands of participants, workshops, hackathons and culture
european-youth-event-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 16–30. The funding call is for groups (with a group leader aged 18+); check the call for country eligibility. Activities in many EU languages, mainly English.
how_to_apply: Read the call for groups on european-youth-event.europarl.europa.eu
Form a group with a leader aged 18+
Submit the group application by 13 November 2026
If not funded, watch the site for open registration for EYE2027
european-youth-event-2027.costs: Participation free. Selected groups receive an EU financial contribution toward travel and accommodation; otherwise costs are your own.

euroscola-european-parliament.about:
Euroscola, created by the European Parliament in 1990, has given hundreds of thousands of high-school students a day as MEPs in the Parliament's chamber in Strasbourg. Students aged at least 14 from the 27 EU member states, the EU candidate countries and former member states debate, take sides, negotiate, amend and vote on resolutions about real European issues, working in multilingual groups.

Sessions run throughout the school year (the next is on 10 November 2026). Schools take part as a class, accompanied by a teacher. Places are allocated through a national selection organised by the European Parliament Liaison Office in each country, often a competition; the Liaison Office also explains the travel-cost reimbursement for selected schools.

It is a free, memorable introduction to EU politics, and a great project for a motivated class and teacher.
highlights: A day as an MEP in the Strasbourg chamber
Open to EU, candidate and former member states
Travel costs reimbursed for selected schools
euroscola-european-parliament.eligibility: Secondary-school students aged 14+, as a class with a teacher, from EU member states, EU candidate countries (for example Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine, Türkiye, Western Balkans) and former member states. Working languages vary; good English or French helps.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher to check the Euroscola 'How to participate' page
Contact the European Parliament Liaison Office for your country about the national selection
Take part in the national competition/selection
If selected, register the class for a session date and prepare on EU basics
euroscola-european-parliament.costs: Free. Travel-cost reimbursement for selected schools is arranged via the Liaison Office.

nvidia-inception.about:
NVIDIA Inception supports startups building with AI, data science, graphics and other accelerated computing. Members get access to technical resources and NVIDIA experts, training through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute, preferred pricing and credits from NVIDIA and cloud partners, co-marketing (badges and social content) and, depending on eligibility, investor exposure through Inception Capital Connect and curated networking events with venture capital firms.

You can apply regardless of your funding stage: there are no application fees, deadlines or cohorts. Submit details about your company and product; NVIDIA reviews it and follows up, and more opportunities unlock as your engagement grows.

Very useful for student founders working on AI products who need GPUs, training and credibility with investors.
highlights: Free, no deadlines, any funding stage
Technical support, training and partner credits
Investor introductions via Inception Capital Connect
nvidia-inception.eligibility: Startups (a company with a website and product focus) working with AI or accelerated computing, at any funding stage, anywhere in the world.
how_to_apply: Go to nvidia.com/startups and click 'Apply to Inception'
Submit details about your business and products
Keep your profile updated to receive offers and event invitations

aws-activate.about:
AWS Activate is Amazon's programme for startups. It offers promotional AWS credits based on your funding stage, up to $200,000, plus additional credits for AI startups ready to scale, together with technical support, training and partner offers. Credits can be used for computing, storage, databases and AI services such as Amazon Bedrock.

Eligibility (as published): pre-Series B, founded in the last 10 years, an AWS account on a paid-tier plan, and being new to Activate credits or requesting a higher tier. Smaller self-funded tiers are open to very early founders, while larger tiers usually require backing from an accelerator, incubator or VC in the Activate network.

Useful for any student founder who needs to host a product without paying for cloud computing.
highlights: Up to $200,000 in AWS credits by stage
Extra credits for AI startups
Rolling, global, online application
aws-activate.eligibility: Startups worldwide that are pre-Series B, founded within the last 10 years, with an AWS paid-tier account; new to Activate or applying for a higher tier.
how_to_apply: Create an AWS account on a paid-tier plan
Go to aws.amazon.com/startups/credits and pick your tier
Submit company details (website, stage, funding)
Credits are applied to your account if approved
aws-activate.costs: Free; credits expire after a set period.

google-for-startups-cloud-program.about:
The Google for Startups Cloud Program supports digital-native startups that are new Google Cloud customers. At the prototyping stage you can get instant access to Google AI Studio to build an MVP. Pre-seed to Series A startups can apply for up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years, credits for frontier models such as Gemini and Gemma, technical and product training (Google Skills), 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus and monthly Google Maps Platform credits. As you grow you can unlock dedicated help from Google's startup experts.

There is no deadline or cohort. It is a simple way for student founders to run AI products at no cost in their first years.
highlights: Up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years
Gemini/Gemma model credits and Workspace for a year
Rolling, online, worldwide
google-for-startups-cloud-program.eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A startups founding digital-native products that are new Google Cloud customers; exact criteria are on the application page. Worldwide.
how_to_apply: Go to cloud.google.com/startup
If you are just prototyping, start free in Google AI Studio
Otherwise click 'Apply to the program' and submit company details
Credits are issued if approved

global-entrepreneurship-week-2026.about:
Global Entrepreneurship Week (GEW) is the world's largest celebration of entrepreneurship. In 2025 it involved about 200 countries, 20,000 partner organisations, 40,000 activities and 10 million people. Universities, incubators, governments, schools and companies run events during the week: startup weekends, pitch competitions, founder talks, mentoring sessions, hackathons and policy roundtables.

GEW 2026 runs from 16 to 22 November 2026. Students can use 'Find an Event' on the GEN website to locate activities near them or online, or use 'Add an Event' to register their own club or school event in the global calendar (with a promotional toolkit and logos). GEN's 'Ideas Bank' and 'Signature Activities' pages give ready-made formats.

It is a free, low-barrier first step into the startup world, and hosting an event is a good leadership project for a student club.
highlights: Free events in ~200 countries, online and in person
Find an event near you or host your own
Pitch nights, workshops, hackathons and founder talks
global-entrepreneurship-week-2026.eligibility: Open to everyone; most events are free. Individual events may have their own age or registration rules.
how_to_apply: Visit genglobal.org/gew
Use 'Find An Event' to pick local or online activities and register
Or click 'Add An Event' to list your own school or club event
Take part during 16–22 November 2026
global-entrepreneurship-week-2026.costs: Free to participate; some partner events may charge.

international-award-for-young-people.about:
The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award (known in many countries as the International Award for Young People) challenges young people to develop themselves through four sections: Voluntary Service, Physical Recreation, Skills and an Adventurous Journey, plus a Gold Residential Project at the top level. Participants choose their own activities and set goals with an adult Award Leader, then record progress in the Online Record Book.

Levels: Bronze (from age 14, at least 6 months, a 2-day/1-night journey); Silver (from 15, at least 12 months, or 6 if you hold Bronze, a 3-day/2-night journey); Gold (from 16, at least 18 months, or 12 if you hold Silver, a 4-day/3-night journey and a residential project). You must finish before your 25th birthday.

The Award is delivered in more than 130 countries, including Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Ukraine, Moldova and most of Europe, through National Award Operators and licensed Independent Award Centres such as international schools and scout groups. It is widely recognised by universities and employers as evidence of commitment and character.
highlights: Recognised by universities and employers worldwide
Bronze, Silver and Gold levels from age 14
Available in 130+ countries via schools and licensed centres
international-award-for-young-people.eligibility: Young people aged 14–24 (Bronze from 14, Silver from 15, Gold from 16; complete before turning 25). You must register through an Award Centre (school, club or organisation) in your country.
how_to_apply: Check 'Find the Award in your country' (intaward.org/do/regions-locations)
Ask your school or a listed Independent Award Centre to enrol you
Choose activities and goals for each section with your Award Leader
Log progress in the Online Record Book and complete your Adventurous Journey
international-award-for-young-people.costs: Participation fees are set by each country or Award Centre and are usually modest; expeditions may have equipment and travel costs.

young-activists-summit-2026.about:
The Young Activists Summit (YAS) is held each year at the Palais des Nations in Geneva. It shines a light on young activists from around the world who are tackling issues such as climate, education, gender equality, health and human rights. Selected activists present their work in short talks and films, and the audience joins discussions with them and with UN and NGO representatives.

The 2026 Summit takes place on 17 December 2026 from 10:00 to 12:00 Geneva time, at the UN in Geneva and online. Registration to attend will open soon; subscribe to the newsletter on the official site to be notified.

It is a free, inspiring event for students interested in activism and international organisations; attending online is open to anyone.
highlights: Held at the United Nations in Geneva
Free to attend in person or online
Showcases young activists from around the world
young-activists-summit-2026.eligibility: Open to the public, especially young people; in-person places are limited and require registration (UN security rules apply). Online viewing is open to all. English.
how_to_apply: Visit youngactivistssummit.org and subscribe for registration news
Register to attend in Geneva or online once registration opens
Bring ID accepted by UN Geneva security if attending in person
young-activists-summit-2026.costs: Free. Travel to Geneva at your own cost.

climate-reality-leadership-corps-budapes.about:
The Climate Reality Project, founded by Al Gore, runs Leadership Corps trainings around the world. Over two immersive days, participants learn the science of the climate crisis and its solutions, how to communicate it persuasively, and how to organise for change, with sessions led by Al Gore and world-class scientists, policy experts and activists.

After the training you become a Climate Reality Leader and join a global network with virtual and in-person community events, online courses and resources. Leaders are expected to take action afterwards, such as giving presentations, organising in their community or engaging decision-makers.

The next listed in-person training is in Budapest, Hungary, in February 2027. The application is not live yet; sign up on the training page to be told when it opens. Other online and in-person trainings are held during the year.
highlights: Training led by Al Gore and top climate experts
Join a global network of Climate Reality Leaders
Historically free to attend (travel your own)
climate-reality-leadership-corps-budapes.eligibility: Adults (normally 18+) of any nationality with a commitment to climate action. English (with interpretation at some trainings). Selection by application.
how_to_apply: Go to climaterealityproject.org/training
Sign up to be notified when the Budapest application goes live
Complete the application describing your climate commitment
If accepted, register and arrange travel to Budapest
climate-reality-leadership-corps-budapes.costs: Training has historically been free of charge; travel, accommodation and visas are at your own cost. Check the application page for current terms.

global-shapers-community.about:
The Global Shapers Community was created by the World Economic Forum for young people driving change in their cities. Shapers are organised in city-based hubs; each hub chooses its own projects (climate, education, civic engagement, mental health, inclusion and more) and runs them as volunteers. Selected Shapers are invited to WEF events such as the Annual Meeting in Davos and the Shaping Davos programme, and the network gives access to peers and leaders worldwide.

Membership is for people under 30 who have shown leadership and commitment to their community. Recruitment is done locally: each hub opens applications on its own schedule, typically once or twice a year, with an application form and interviews. Hubs exist in many capitals and large cities (for example Tbilisi and Doha).

Find your nearest hub on the official site and follow it on social media to catch the next recruitment round.
highlights: 11,000+ members in 450 hubs and 140 countries
Run local impact projects with peers
Chance to join World Economic Forum events
global-shapers-community.eligibility: Young people under 30 (most hubs recruit roughly 18–27) living in or near a hub's city, with demonstrated leadership and community impact. English plus local language.
how_to_apply: Open globalshapers.org/hubs and find the hub in your city
Follow the hub's channels for its next recruitment call
Submit the hub's application (motivation, CV, project ideas)
Attend an interview with current Shapers
global-shapers-community.costs: Free membership; members volunteer their time.

discovereu-spring-2027.about:
DiscoverEU lets young Europeans discover the continent's diversity, cultural heritage and history and meet people from all over Europe. Selected travellers receive a travel pass (mostly rail, with alternatives for islands and remote areas) to travel for up to 30 days, alone or in a group of up to five, plus a European Youth Card with discounts on culture, accommodation and food. Many national agencies also organise pre-departure meetings and meet-ups.

There are two application rounds a year (spring and autumn). The autumn 2026 round is closed; the next round, in spring 2027, is open to people born between 1 July 2008 and 30 June 2009. Applicants answer a short quiz about the EU and a tie-breaker question. From 2027 the United Kingdom joins Erasmus+, including DiscoverEU.

It is the easiest way for an 18-year-old in Europe to travel for free and is excellent for independence and languages.
highlights: Free travel pass for up to 30 days
European Youth Card discounts
Two rounds a year; UK joins from 2027
discovereu-spring-2027.eligibility: Aged 18 (spring 2027: born 1 July 2008 – 30 June 2009) and a citizen or legal resident of an EU member state or a third country associated to Erasmus+ (Iceland, Liechtenstein, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Türkiye; the UK from 2027). Not open to other countries (e.g. Georgia or Qatar).
how_to_apply: Check youth.europa.eu/discovereu_en for the spring 2027 dates
Log in with an EU Login account when the round opens
Complete the quiz and tie-breaker question
If selected, plan your itinerary and book your pass
discovereu-spring-2027.costs: Travel pass is free (funded by Erasmus+). Accommodation, food and other costs are your own, with Youth Card discounts.

leangap-summer-2027.about:
Leangap is a startup accelerator for high-school students. Teams of ambitious peers from around the world go through a full-time programme: classes in the morning, team project work for the rest of the day, mentoring by founders and technologists, and a final pitch to real investors. No prior business or coding experience is required.

Summer 2027 options: Online, 14 June to 9 July 2027 (four weeks plus a prep week), US$6,450; San Francisco, 11 July to 7 August 2027, US$14,950 including housing, all meals and airport transfers. Need-based scholarships give 10–80% off the online programme and 10–50% off the San Francisco programme (no full rides), based on parents' income statements.

It is expensive compared with free options such as LaunchX's competitions or the Diamond Challenge, but it is one of the few programmes where teenagers actually launch a company over the summer.
highlights: Build and launch a real startup in four weeks
Pitch to actual investors at the end
Online or in San Francisco; partial scholarships
leangap-summer-2027.eligibility: High-school students worldwide; no prior experience in business or coding needed. English.
how_to_apply: Go to leangap.org and click 'Apply for Summer 2027'
Choose Online or San Francisco
Complete the application (and the scholarship request with income documents if needed)
If admitted, pay the $700 non-refundable deposit to hold your place
leangap-summer-2027.costs: Online: US$6,450. San Francisco: US$14,950 (housing, meals, airport transfers included). $700 deposit (non-refundable, counts toward tuition). Need-based discounts of 10–80% (online) or 10–50% (SF).

techstars-london-2027.about:
Techstars London backs emerging startups from all over the world and across all verticals, using London's diversity, global outlook and talent.

The 2027 programme timeline: applications opened 24 August 2026; final deadline 18 November 2026; the accelerator starts on 8 March 2027 and ends with Demo Day on 3 June 2027. Founders work intensively with the managing director, dozens of mentors and the Techstars network to reach product-market fit and prepare to raise funding.

Techstars invests $220,000 in each company, made up of two components (see the programme FAQ for terms), and companies receive more than $2 million in partner perks, access to Techstars' investor, mentor and alumni network, and lifetime support. Student founders with a working product and a committed team can apply; the programme is in English.
highlights: $220,000 investment per company
Three months of mentor-driven acceleration
Demo Day on 3 June 2027 and lifetime network access
techstars-london-2027.eligibility: Startup teams of any nationality with a product or strong prototype; founders are expected to work full-time on the company during the programme and be in the city as required. English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and FAQ on techstars.com
Apply at apply.techstars.com by 18 November 2026
Interview with the managing director and team if shortlisted
Accepted companies sign the investment documents and start on 8 March 2027
techstars-london-2027.costs: No fee. Techstars invests $220,000 in exchange for equity (two components; see FAQ). Relocation and living costs are the founders' own.

techstars-new-york-city-2027.about:
Techstars New York City is a sector-agnostic programme that aims to compress two years of work into three months, in the heart of the US's largest startup and investor ecosystem.

The 2027 programme timeline: applications opened 24 August 2026; final deadline 18 November 2026; the accelerator starts on 8 March 2027 and ends with Demo Day on 3 June 2027. Founders work intensively with the managing director, dozens of mentors and the Techstars network to reach product-market fit and prepare to raise funding.

Techstars invests $220,000 in each company, made up of two components (see the programme FAQ for terms), and companies receive more than $2 million in partner perks, access to Techstars' investor, mentor and alumni network, and lifetime support. Student founders with a working product and a committed team can apply; the programme is in English.
highlights: $220,000 investment per company
Three months of mentor-driven acceleration
Demo Day on 3 June 2027 and lifetime network access
techstars-new-york-city-2027.eligibility: Startup teams of any nationality with a product or strong prototype; founders are expected to work full-time on the company during the programme and be in the city as required. English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and FAQ on techstars.com
Apply at apply.techstars.com by 18 November 2026
Interview with the managing director and team if shortlisted
Accepted companies sign the investment documents and start on 8 March 2027
techstars-new-york-city-2027.costs: No fee. Techstars invests $220,000 in exchange for equity (two components; see FAQ). Relocation and living costs are the founders' own.

techstars-boston-2027.about:
Techstars Boston, one of the network's original programmes, works with ambitious founders and gives them what they need to accelerate their growth, close to Boston's universities and investors.

The 2027 programme timeline: applications opened 24 August 2026; final deadline 18 November 2026; the accelerator starts on 8 March 2027 and ends with Demo Day on 3 June 2027. Founders work intensively with the managing director, dozens of mentors and the Techstars network to reach product-market fit and prepare to raise funding.

Techstars invests $220,000 in each company, made up of two components (see the programme FAQ for terms), and companies receive more than $2 million in partner perks, access to Techstars' investor, mentor and alumni network, and lifetime support. highlights: $220,000 investment per company
Three months of mentor-driven acceleration
Demo Day on 3 June 2027 and lifetime network access

Apply at apply.techstars.com by 18 November 2026
Interview with the managing director and team if shortlisted
