rice-business-plan-competition-2027.about:
The Rice Business Plan Competition (RBPC), now in its 27th year, is organised by the Rice Alliance and Rice University's Jones Graduate School of Business. It showcases the best student startups from around the world: about 40 teams are invited to Houston to pitch to hundreds of investors and judges, receive mentoring and compete in multiple rounds.

More than $1 million in investment and cash prizes is expected in 2027, and every invited startup receives a minimum prize (all teams win cash in the Wildcard round). Timeline: applications open 9 November 2026; an info webinar in December; applications close 29 January 2027; invitations announced 16 February 2027; competition on 8–10 April 2027 at Rice University.

RBPC is ideal for university founders with a real startup (many are graduate students), and alumni have collectively raised billions.
highlights: $1M+ in cash and investment prizes; every team wins something
About 40 student startups from around the world
Pitch to hundreds of investors in Houston
rice-business-plan-competition-2027.eligibility: Startups that are student-driven, -created or -managed, with at least two current student founders or managers at any university in the world; under $300,000 equity raised before 1 July 2026 and under $150,000 revenue in any 12 months (see the 2027 eligibility document). English.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 Eligibility and How to Apply document on rbpc.rice.edu/eligibility
Prepare your executive summary, pitch deck and team details
Apply between 9 November 2026 and 29 January 2027
If invited (16 Feb 2027), confirm by 22 Feb and travel to Houston for 8–10 April
rice-business-plan-competition-2027.costs: Free to apply. Check the rules for travel and accommodation support for invited teams.

yale-young-global-scholars-2027.about:
Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) brings outstanding high-school students from more than 150 countries to Yale's campus for a two-week interdisciplinary session. Sessions (such as Politics, Law and Economics; Biological and Biomedical Science; Applied Science and Engineering; International Affairs and Security; Literature, Philosophy and Culture; Solving Global Challenges; Sustainability, Energy and Environment) combine lectures by Yale faculty, seminars, small-group discussions and a capstone project. For 2027 all sessions are residential, in June and July.

Application: Early Action closed on 15 October 2026; Regular Decision closes at 11:59 pm ET on 6 January 2027 (fee $100, fee waivers available), with decisions by mid-March. Tuition is $7,500 for a two-week session, covering housing, meals and materials, but not travel. Need-based financial aid is available to students from all countries and can cover up to 100% of tuition.

YYGS is one of the most international pre-college leadership programmes, and its alumni network is highly valued.
highlights: Two weeks at Yale with students from 150+ countries
Need-based aid up to 100% of tuition, open to all countries
Leadership, debate and capstone projects with Yale faculty
yale-young-global-scholars-2027.eligibility: Current high-school sophomores or juniors (or international equivalent) graduating in May/June 2028 or 2029 (Northern Hemisphere) or Nov/Dec 2027 or 2028 (Southern Hemisphere); fluent in English; first-time participants. Students from all countries may apply.
how_to_apply: Read eligibility and session offerings on globalscholars.yale.edu
Complete the online application (essays, transcript, recommendation)
Request financial aid in the application if needed
Submit by 6 January 2027 and pay the $100 fee (or request a waiver)
Decisions by mid-March 2027; pay tuition by 15 March for admits
yale-young-global-scholars-2027.costs: Tuition $7,500 (2-week residential session, housing and meals included; travel not covered). Application fee $100 (Regular Decision). Need-based aid up to 100% of tuition.

imagine-cup-2027.about:
The Imagine Cup is Microsoft's long-running global competition for student entrepreneurs. Teams build a startup around an AI-powered product on Microsoft's cloud, progress through online rounds and semifinals judged by industry experts, and the top three teams compete in the World Championship for the title and prizes, with mentoring and Azure resources along the way. Recent champions include Argus (2025) and FROM YOUR EYES from Türkiye (2024). The 2026 edition was organised around 'Innovate. Validate. Accelerate.'

The official site currently announces 'Imagine Cup 2027 – Coming Soon!'. Registration dates, eligibility and prizes will be published on imaginecup.microsoft.com; historically, registration opened in the autumn and submissions closed in winter, with the World Championship in spring.

It is one of the few big-company startup competitions designed specifically for students, and a good target for university teams already building with AI.
highlights: Global competition for student startups using AI
Mentoring, Azure credits and a World Championship
Past champions from Türkiye and around the world
imagine-cup-2027.eligibility: University students (age 16+, enrolled at an accredited institution) in eligible countries, in teams; final 2027 rules will be published on the official site.
how_to_apply: Watch imaginecup.microsoft.com for the 2027 launch
Form a team and pick an AI-powered startup idea
Register and use Microsoft for Startups resources and Azure credits
Submit your pitch and product demo for the first round

nfte-world-series-of-innovation-2027.about:
The World Series of Innovation (WSI) is run by NFTE, a US non-profit that teaches entrepreneurship to young people. Each year companies and foundations sponsor challenges linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and participants submit an innovative product, service or business idea, individually or in teams.

2026–27 challenges: Imagination League (ages 5–12): Aflatoun Kidpreneurs Challenge and MetLife Foundation Good Health & Well-Being Challenge. Impact League (ages 13–24): EverBank Smart Hustle Challenge, MetLife Foundation Good Health & Well-Being Challenge, Fifth Third Bank Skills for Success Challenge, Intuit Food Truck Innovation Challenge and EY Responsible AI Challenge. Submissions are due 13 December 2026 at innovation.nfte.com; winners are announced in spring 2027 and receive $300–$1,500.

It is free, open worldwide and accepts submissions in English, Spanish, Arabic, Simplified Chinese and Hindi, with free learning resources for students and teachers, which makes it a very accessible first entrepreneurship competition.
highlights: Free and open to ages 5–24 worldwide
Submit in English, Arabic, Spanish, Chinese or Hindi
Cash prizes $300–$1,500 in each challenge
nfte-world-series-of-innovation-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 5–24 anywhere in the world, individually or in teams (younger participants with an adult/teacher). Submissions in English, Spanish, Arabic, Simplified Chinese or Hindi.
how_to_apply: Go to innovation.nfte.com and read the challenge briefs and rules
Pick a challenge in your age league (5–12 or 13–24)
Develop your idea using the free learning resources
Submit online by 13 December 2026

a16z-speedrun.about:
speedrun is the accelerator of Andreessen Horowitz, one of the world's largest venture firms. Selected teams receive a first check of up to $1 million (with a target two-week close), more than $10 million in credits from 200+ partners, and help with customers and hiring. The residency runs in person at a16z's San Francisco office for sessions, office hours and events, and founders are expected to build full-time. Solo founders can apply; traction is not required, though early signs that people want the product help.

Applications for the SR008 residency were open 12 October – 1 November 2026. If you miss the window, you can still apply and your application is reviewed for the next residency.

For students, recent graduates and dropouts still finding their idea, a16z runs a separate 'alpha fellowship' (up to $250K, US work authorisation required); its current cycle closed on 11 October.
highlights: Up to $1M investment with a two-week close
$10M+ in partner credits
In-person residency in San Francisco; solo founders welcome
a16z-speedrun.eligibility: Founders building full-time with an idea, early product and team (solo founders allowed), any sector, any nationality; must be able to attend in San Francisco.
how_to_apply: Read the FAQ at speedrun.a16z.com/faq
Apply at speedrun.a16z.com/apply with team bios and deck
Applications after 1 Nov 2026 are reviewed for the next residency
Shortlisted teams interview with an investing partner
a16z-speedrun.costs: No fee. a16z invests in exchange for equity. Living and travel costs are the founders'.

mit-mites-summer-2027.about:
MITES Summer is MIT's flagship six-week residential STEM programme for rising high-school seniors. Around 80 students live in MIT dormitories and take five courses (typically a maths course, a physics or life-science course, a humanities course, and project-based electives such as engineering design or computer science) taught by MIT-affiliated instructors, with recitations, workshops, lab tours and a written evaluation from each instructor at the end.

The programme targets talented students from communities under-represented in science and engineering, including first-generation, low-income and rural students. Classes run weekdays 9:00 to 17:00; evenings and weekends bring social events and trips around Greater Boston, plus college-admissions counselling.

It is entirely free: MIT and its donors cover tuition, housing and meals, and students pay only travel to and from campus. Admission is very competitive and is a strong signal on university applications. Note: only US citizens and permanent residents are eligible; international students should look at other programmes in this list.
highlights: Completely free six weeks on MIT's campus, including room and board
Five college-level courses plus admissions counselling and written instructor evaluations
Strong alumni network: many MITES alumni go on to MIT and other top universities
mit-mites-summer-2027.eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents (green card) in 11th grade at the time of application; public, private and home-schooled students welcome. Students may not apply from outside the US. Priority is given to students from under-represented and under-resourced backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Check the MITES website in mid-November 2026, when the 2027 MITES Summer/Semester application opens on the MITES portal
Prepare essays, transcript and activity information
Ask your recommenders early: recommendation requests must be sent by 1 February, and letters are due by mid-February
Submit the online application by 1 February 2027, 11:59 pm PT
Decisions arrive in spring; admitted students attend the residential programme in summer 2027
mit-mites-summer-2027.costs: Free. Tuition, on-campus housing and meals are covered by MIT and donors. Students pay only their own travel to and from MIT and personal expenses. No application fee is mentioned.

clark-scholars-program-2027.about:
The Anson L. Clark Scholars Program is an intensive seven-week summer research programme at Texas Tech University for twelve highly qualified rising high-school seniors and recent graduates. Each scholar joins a faculty research group in a field of their choice (sciences, engineering, mathematics, humanities, business and more) and works on a real project, ending with a written research report.

Alongside research, scholars attend weekly seminars, social activities and weekend programming, and live together on campus. With only a dozen places nationwide, it is one of the most selective pre-college programmes in the United States and carries real weight in university admissions.

There is no participation fee: on-campus housing, meals and weekend activities are provided, and each scholar receives a $750 stipend after submitting a successful research report. The programme is open only to US citizens and permanent residents.
highlights: Only 12 scholars selected: extremely prestigious
Free housing and meals plus a $750 stipend
Real one-to-one research with Texas Tech faculty in many disciplines
clark-scholars-program-2027.eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents, at least 17 years old by the programme start date, graduating high school in 2027 or 2028 (i.e. participating the summer before senior year or right after graduation). No exceptions.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 research areas and essay prompts on the Clark Scholars website (you can draft essays before the portal opens)
Create an account when the application opens on 2 January 2027
Upload unofficial transcripts and SAT/ACT (or at least PSAT/PreACT) score reports
Enter three recommenders (at least two teachers); they complete an online questionnaire by the deadline
List your top five activities, pay the $25 fee and submit by 15 February 2027, 11:59 pm CT
clark-scholars-program-2027.costs: No programme fee. On-campus room, meals and weekend activities are provided; $750 stipend on completion of the research report. Students pay the $25 application fee, travel, personal and medical expenses.

simons-summer-research-program-2027.about:
The Simons Summer Research Program gives academically talented high-school juniors the chance to do real research in science, mathematics or engineering at Stony Brook University. Simons Fellows are matched with faculty mentors in chemistry, computer science, geosciences, marine science, neurobiology and more than a dozen other departments, join active research teams, learn laboratory techniques and pursue a question of their own.

The 2027 programme runs 28 June to 6 August 2027 and ends with a research poster symposium. Prior research experience is not required, but the programme is highly selective: 1,864 students applied in 2026 and fewer than 5% are admitted. Many fellows go on to become Regeneron Science Talent Search scholars.

Applicants must be nominated by their school (up to three students per school) and rank three preferred mentors or research areas. There is no tuition, but residential participants pay for housing and meals.
highlights: Real lab research with Stony Brook faculty mentors
No tuition or programme fee
Strong track record of Regeneron STS scholars
simons-summer-research-program-2027.eligibility: High-school juniors (11th grade) at the time of application, US citizens or permanent residents only (no visa holders), at least 16 by the programme start, and nominated by their school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to submit a nomination by 29 January 2027 (max. three students per school)
Open the online application after it is posted on 15 November 2026
Upload your transcript, write short responses (max. 300 words each, no AI-generated text) and rank three mentors from the mentor list
Pay the $75 fee (waivers for financial hardship) and submit by 5 February 2027, 11:59 pm EST
Teacher recommendations are due 12 February 2027; decisions are emailed in early April
simons-summer-research-program-2027.costs: No tuition or programme fee. Residential participants pay for housing and dining; commuters pay their own transport and meals. Application fee US$75 (waivers available).

stanford-simr-2027.about:
SIMR places about 50 high-school students in Stanford Medicine research labs for eight weeks. Students choose an institute or research area (such as immunology, stem cells and regenerative medicine, neuroscience, cancer biology, cardiovascular medicine, bioengineering or genetics/genomics), work on a project under a mentor, attend lectures by Stanford faculty, and present a poster at the end of the summer.

The tentative 2027 dates are 7 June to 29 July 2027. The programme exists to give students, especially those from groups under-represented in medicine and science, early exposure to biomedical research.

There is no cost for selected students and a few need-based stipends are available, but housing is not provided: participants must live with a parent or relative, and selection heavily favours local Bay Area students. Only US citizens or permanent residents living in and attending high school in the US may apply.
highlights: Eight weeks in a Stanford Medicine lab with a research mentor
No programme cost; limited need-based stipends
Poster session and lectures from Stanford faculty
stanford-simr-2027.eligibility: Juniors or seniors (class of 2027 or 2028), aged 16+ by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the US, and US citizens or green-card holders. Local (Bay Area) students are strongly favoured; students must arrange housing with a family member.
how_to_apply: Read the SIMR mission and FAQ pages carefully, especially the housing rule
Download the programme information and application when posted on 18 December 2026
Choose your preferred institutes/research areas and write the essays
Pay the $50 fee (waived for family income under $80,000) and submit by the late-February 2027 deadline
stanford-simr-2027.costs: No cost for selected students. Application fee US$50 (waivers available). No housing or transport provided; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist.

shad-canada-2027.about:
Shad is a 27-day summer programme hosted on partner university campuses across Canada (for example Calgary, Western in London, and others; the list varies by year). Students in Grade 10 or 11 live in residence and learn across five interdisciplinary areas, from AI, robotics and biomedical engineering to design, entrepreneurship and the humanities, through lectures, labs, field trips and a team design-and-entrepreneurship challenge. A virtual option runs 5–30 July 2027.

With over 20,000 alumni, Shad is a respected name for Canadian university and scholarship applications, and its alumni network is a big part of the value. The 2027 on-campus programme runs 4–30 July 2027.

Fees for 2027 are CA$7,875 (live-in) or CA$3,975 (virtual) for Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with up to the full fee covered for low-income families. International students can apply but pay CA$12,475 (live-in) or CA$6,750 (virtual) and are not eligible for Shad's financial aid.
highlights: A month living on a Canadian university campus with top students
Team challenge combining STEAM and entrepreneurship
Large alumni network; CA$5 million in fee assistance yearly for Canadians
shad-canada-2027.eligibility: High-school students currently in Grade 10 or 11 (Secondaire IV or V in Quebec). Open to all nationalities; non-Canadians (no citizenship, PR or refugee status) pay the international fee and cannot receive Shad financial aid.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Shad's application page (free to apply)
Optionally submit by 8 November 2026 for an early decision and a guaranteed top-10 campus choice
Complete the written responses, activity information and references
Submit by 6 January 2027, 11:59 pm ET; decisions arrive in the first week of February
If admitted, pay a CA$750 deposit; the balance is paid in two instalments
shad-canada-2027.costs: 2027 fees: domestic CA$7,875 live-in / CA$3,975 virtual (need-based assistance up to the full fee); international CA$12,475 live-in / CA$6,750 virtual, no aid. The live-in fee covers programme, residence, meals and activities; travel is extra.

cern-beamline-for-schools-2027.about:
Beamline for Schools (BL4S) invites teams of high-school students from anywhere in the world to propose an experiment that uses a particle beam. Teams (with a teacher or adult coach) write a proposal of up to about 1,000 words and a one-minute video explaining their idea, from testing detectors to measuring particle properties or materials science.

Proposals for the 2027 edition can be submitted from December 2026 until 12 March 2027. CERN scientists shortlist the best and the winning teams are announced in June; they then work with physicists to plan their experiment and spend roughly two weeks in late September 2027 at CERN (Geneva), DESY (Hamburg) or ELSA (Bonn), with travel, accommodation and meals fully covered.

Since 2014 thousands of teams from over 100 countries have entered. Even non-winning teams can earn special prizes (up to 50 teams), video awards and participation certificates. It is completely free and a superb project for a school physics club.
highlights: Run your own experiment on a real particle-accelerator beamline
Free to enter; winners' travel, accommodation and meals fully covered
Open to secondary-school teams worldwide, with online events from November 2026
cern-beamline-for-schools-2027.eligibility: Teams of secondary-school students (typically at least five members) from any country, supervised by a coach aged 18+ (usually a teacher). Students must be at least 16 to travel to CERN/DESY/ELSA if they win; younger students may take part in the proposal stage. Proposals are written in English.
how_to_apply: Form a team and find a coach (teacher or adult mentor)
Attend the online information events from November 2026 and read the 2027 invitation and proposal guidelines
Write your experiment proposal and record the short video
Submit via the BL4S website between December 2026 and 12 March 2027 (23:59 CET)
Winners are notified in June 2027 and travel in late September 2027
cern-beamline-for-schools-2027.costs: Free to participate. For winning teams BL4S covers travel, accommodation and three meals a day.

oxford-uniq-2027.about:
UNIQ is the University of Oxford's flagship widening-participation programme, running since 2010 and working with more than a thousand students a year. Participants attend a regional event in spring, then a one-week subject-specific residential in Oxford in late June or July (Monday to Friday), living in a college, attending lectures and tutorials, and experiencing student life.

After the residential, UNIQ provides sustained online support from August to December to help participants make a competitive Oxford application, including help with admissions tests and interviews. Subjects span sciences, engineering, maths, medicine, humanities and social sciences.

The programme is completely free. It prioritises students with good grades from backgrounds under-represented at Oxford, but is open only to students at UK state schools; international students are not eligible.
highlights: One week living and studying in an Oxford college, all costs covered
Wide range of subjects with Oxford tutors
Ongoing support for the Oxford application, admissions tests and interview
oxford-uniq-2027.eligibility: Students at UK state schools in Year 12 (England and Wales), Year 13 (Northern Ireland) or S5 (Scotland) with strong grades. Priority for students from under-represented backgrounds (e.g. low-income, first-generation, care-experienced, areas with low progression to university). Not open to international or independent-school students.
how_to_apply: Register on the UNIQ website to be told when the 2027 application opens in December 2026
Check the selection criteria and choose a course
Complete the online application (only through the UNIQ website)
Submit before the January 2027 deadline; late applications are never accepted
Accept your place within a week of the February decision email
oxford-uniq-2027.costs: Completely free: accommodation, meals, academic programme and travel to Oxford are covered.

iowa-sstp-2027.about:
SSTP is a five-and-a-half-week research programme run by the University of Iowa's Belin-Blank Center for gifted students. Each participant joins a faculty research group and completes a project, ending with a research poster. Research departments for 2027 range from biochemistry, genetics, neuroscience and microbiology to chemical, civil, electrical and mechanical engineering, business analytics, psychology and even religious studies.

Students live on campus, attend classes and events designed to build research and academic skills, and earn three semester hours of University of Iowa credit. The 2027 programme runs 16 June to 23 July 2027 and students must commit to the whole period.

The programme fee is US$7,500 (room, board, materials, activities and credit included). Merit- and need-based aid can cover up to 95% of costs and is applied for after acceptance. International students are welcome: they need proof of English proficiency on acceptance and a US visa; the centre buys their health insurance and provides transport from Cedar Rapids airport.
highlights: Real research in a university lab with a faculty mentor
Three semester hours of University of Iowa credit
Open to international students; aid up to 95% of costs
iowa-sstp-2027.eligibility: High-school students in grades 10–11 at the time of application, from any country. SAT or ACT scores are required. International students must show English proficiency (residency in some countries satisfies this) if admitted and obtain a student visa. Students may attend SSTP only once.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 research areas and programme expectations
Open the online application from 15 December 2026 and enter your details
Pay the US$95 fee (waivers on request) and nominate two referees (one academic, one character)
Write two essays (research interests; motivation and career goals, max. 750 words each), upload your transcript and SAT/ACT scores
Submit everything, including references, by 16 February 2027; decisions on 1 April 2027
iowa-sstp-2027.costs: Programme fee US$7,500 including room, board, materials, activities and three credit hours; travel and incidentals extra. Need- and merit-based aid up to 95% of costs, applied for after admission. Application fee US$95 (waivable).

wolfram-high-school-summer-research-2027.about:
The Wolfram High School Summer Research Program is an intensive two-and-a-half-week residential programme that turns motivated high-school students into computational researchers. After workshops and lectures on the Wolfram Language, computational thinking and AI, each student carries out a personal research project, selected in collaboration with Stephen Wolfram and supported by a mentor, and publishes it at the end. Past projects range from cellular automata and molecular modelling to linguistics and image processing.

The 2027 programme takes place at Bentley University in Waltham, near Boston, from 28 June to 17 July 2027. Coding experience is not required: admissions value problem-solving, creativity and maturity. Strong participants can continue in the Wolfram Emerging Leaders Program or join the teaching team.

The fee is US$6,500 including room, board and a year of access to Wolfram technologies. Need-based aid on a sliding scale covers up to 90% of programme costs (not travel or the US$500 deposit). International students are welcome but must obtain their own visa.
highlights: Original, publishable research project chosen with Stephen Wolfram
No coding experience needed; strong mentoring
International students accepted; aid up to 90%
wolfram-high-school-summer-research-2027.eligibility: Students aged 14–17 (exceptional 13-year-olds sometimes accepted; nobody who turns 18 during the programme). Any STEM background; open to international students, who must obtain any necessary visa.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it opens in early November 2026, including short responses on past projects and alumni projects
Request financial aid within the application if needed (no aid requests after 23 April)
Do the video interview with the Admissions Director
Apply by 18 January 2027 (Early Decision, results by 15 Feb) or 15 March 2027 (Regular, results by 23 April)
Pay the US$500 deposit to confirm; the balance is due by 10 May 2027
wolfram-high-school-summer-research-2027.costs: US$6,500 including room, board and a one-year Wolfram licence; includes a non-refundable US$500 deposit. Need-based aid up to 90% of programme costs; travel not covered.

pioneer-research-institute-2027.about:
Pioneer pairs high-school students with professors from research universities for a rigorous, independent research project in almost any field: mathematics, physics, computer science, biology, economics, psychology, history, philosophy and more. Students work in small seminar groups and one-to-one with their professor, and finish with an original research paper evaluated to university standards.

The programme is fully online, so students can take part from any country. Students with passing grades earn four transferable college credits awarded via Pioneer's partnership with Oberlin College, and outstanding papers can be published in the Pioneer Research Journal.

Tuition is US$7,465 (plus, in some cases, a lab/materials fee of up to 2%). Pioneer has awarded about US$14.9 million in need-based scholarships since 2014; these are available where family need can be verified or through partner schools and non-profits. Applications for 2027 are open now.
highlights: One-to-one research with a university professor, fully online
Four transferable college credits via Oberlin College
Need-based scholarships up to full tuition
pioneer-research-institute-2027.eligibility: Current high-school students (grades 9–12) from any country. Strong academic record and English ability for university-level reading and writing; standardised tests optional.
how_to_apply: Attend an online information session (optional)
Register on the Pioneer application portal and choose research areas
Upload an unofficial transcript and invite your counsellor to support at least a week before submitting
Submit by 13 December 2026 for the Spring-through-Summer term, or by the Summer-term deadline announced in January 2027
Request a need-based scholarship in the application if needed
pioneer-research-institute-2027.costs: Tuition US$7,465 (possible lab/materials fee up to 2%). Need-based scholarships available where need can be verified; full-scholarship students pay a refundable deposit.

ucsb-research-mentorship-program-2027.about:
The Research Mentorship Program places high-achieving high-school students with a UCSB mentor for an intensive, individual research project in fields across the sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities. Students attend research-methods classes and the GRIT talks lecture series, write a research paper and present their findings at a closing symposium, earning UC credit.

The 2027 programme runs 14 June to 31 July 2027, beginning with a short virtual component (14–17 June). Students may live in a UCSB residence hall with other pre-college students or commute.

It is a paid programme: 2026 costs were US$5,675 for commuters and US$13,274 for residential students (tuition plus housing and meals); 2027 pricing is published in early December. A limited number of need-based scholarships are available, with priority for California residents. International students are welcome and do not need TOEFL/IELTS scores.
highlights: One-to-one mentored research and a final symposium
University credit from UC Santa Barbara
No English test needed for international applicants

kcl-pre-university-summer-school-2027.about:
King's College London's Pre-University Summer School gives students in their final three years of high school a taste of studying at a leading London university. Each course lasts one week and mixes lectures, seminars, discussion groups, simulations and guest speakers; students can take one, two or three courses across four sessions in July 2027.

Students get a King's certificate of participation and a social programme.

It suits international students who want to test a subject before applying to UK universities. Residential students live in single en-suite rooms at Stamford Street Apartments with 24-hour supervision, breakfast and dinner. No scholarships are advertised.

Students choose one of six 'taster' courses taught by Warwick staff: Arts, Culture and Society; Economics and Finance; Business, Management and Marketing; Health, Medical and Life Sciences; Science and Engineering; or Social Sciences. sciences-po-pre-college-2027.about:
Sciences Po's on-campus Pre-College Programme introduces secondary-school students to the disciplines and methods of one of Europe's leading social-science universities. Over two and a half weeks (35 contact hours) all students take the same core courses in the social sciences, joined by smaller tutorial groups that teach the Sciences Po method, plus master classes and an elective. The 2027 programme runs 3–20 July 2027 in central Paris.

For those who cannot travel, Sciences Po also runs an online two-week World Climate Negotiations Bootcamp, where students role-play international climate negotiations and learn international-relations theory.

Admission is selective but rolling, with decisions about a month after a complete application. 2026 fees were €6,000 (on campus: courses, materials, local transport; no accommodation) and €2,000 (online), plus a €50 application fee. Sciences Po offers no scholarships.

harvard-secondary-school-program-2027.about:
Harvard's Secondary School Program (distinct from its two-week Pre-College Program) lets motivated high-school students enrol in college-level Harvard Summer School courses taught by Harvard or visiting faculty, alongside college students and adults from around the world. Students earn a letter grade and a Harvard transcript.

In 2027 there are two four-week sessions (14 June–8 July and 12 July–5 August; one 4-credit course, about 20 courses to choose from) and a seven-week session (21 June–6 August; one or two courses from more than 200, spanning molecular biology, psychology, computer science, economics, law, entrepreneurship and more). Students can live on campus, commute or study online, with activities, tutoring and a writing centre.

2027 costs range from US$4,180 (one online or commuting course) to US$9,260 (4-week residential) and US$15,980 (7-week residential with two courses), plus a US$75 application fee. Need-based aid is available, but for residential students it is limited to US citizens and permanent residents; Harvard sponsors visas for international residential and commuting students.
